synopsis: The Sukaku clan was a distinguished family of shamans, known for protecting mankind from divine beasts. The elder brother Mutsuki excelled at spiritual magic and the family had high hopes for his future. But his sister Uzuki lacked any sort of spiritual power. According to the family tradition, "If you are not shaman, then you are not a Sukaku." And so Uzuki was imprisoned in the house. Mutsuki wanted freedom for his sister, but he realized that if that they could not escape, then they would have to fight, even if that means they have to overcome his own family.……! For the sake of his sister, the big brother will stand up in an unprecedented "home" revolution fantasy! (Source: Sunday Webry, translated)

synopsis: "Hey Kuroya-kun, you like me, right?" "H-How did you know!?" For an introverted high school boy like Kuroya, revealing his unrequited love would be an embarrassment worse than death. Especially when his crush is a beautiful, popular girl like Kasumi Shiramori, his senpai in the Literature Club. Even though they spend time together in the Literature Club, he had tried to keep his feelings hidden, until now...! Senpai asks the despairing Kuroya, "So── for now, as a trial, would you like to go out with me?" No way. I didn't think it was possible to have a relationship with her!? This can't really be happening── It's a romantic comedy full of sweet flirtation and sadistic teasing from the senpai of your dreams! (Source: SB Creative, translated) Note: Chapter count includes an omake and two bonus chapters.

title: Mimi's Tales of Terror
titleNative: ミミの怪談
synonyms: Las historias de fantasmas de Mimi
synopsis: University student Mimi and her boyfriend Naoto encounter one chilling mystery after another. There’s the enigmatic neighbor woman dressed in black from head to toe—but if she’s so odd, why does it seems like there are many others like her? Then, whose eyes track Mimi’s movements from the cemetery next door? And why does a bizarre red circle drawn on a basement wall change with each passing day? Nine scary stories that really happened, drawn from the famed collection of urban legends Shin Mimibukuro (New Earmuffs), and adapted into manga by horror genius Junji Ito! Chapter 1: On the Utility Pole Chapter 2: The Woman Next Door Chapter 3: Rustling in the Grass Chapter 4: Grave Placement Chapter 5: Seashore Chapter 6: Just the Two of Us Chapter 7: Scarlet Circle Chapter 8: Sign in the Field Chapter 9: Monster Prop (Source: VIZ Media)

synopsis: Your "welcome home" is the perfect remedy. Tsukasa Shiozaki has secretly been in love with Yukihito Kuze, a regular at the restaurant where he works who often comes in with his girlfriend. Watching them look so happy together always reminds Tsukasa that his feelings are one-sided, and he's long since given up on confessing. But one day everything changes. “If you don't have anywhere to go, why not come to my place?” With that sudden invitation made to Yukihito, Tsukasa’s ordinary life takes an unexpected turn. (Source: Kadokawa, translated) Notes: - All chapters were split into two parts in the original serialization and later combined in the volume releases. All Bangai-hen (番外編) published on Pixiv Comic were not included in any of the volumes. - Includes five extra chapters.
